sectionProgressions.description: Six-beat metric cycle (4 beats of heavy riff + 2 beats of resolving chord stabs)
Massive wall of overdriven guitars under Chris Cornell's soaring vocal hook
Ascending power-chord tension leading into Kim Thayil's microtonal wah-wah solo

harmonicFunction: Em (i) - Heavy, somber tonic anchor rumbling on the open low E string
G (♭III) - Blues-rock minor third lift providing forward motion
C (♭VI) - Dark submediant chord completing the natural minor cadence
A (IV) - Major IV chord injecting bright Dorian color in the chorus

techniques.name: 6/4 Time Signature Groove & Sludgy Palm Mutes
techniques.description: Internalizing the 6-beat measure (subdivided as 4/4 followed by a 2/4 measure) while playing heavy, sludgy low E palm-muted riffing

notes: Main riff on low E: Open E → fret 3 (G) → fret 2 (F#) → fret 3 on A string (C) → fret 2 on A (B)
Counting: 1-2-3-4 (riff) then 1-2 (chord stab) = 6 beats per measure
Chorus open chords: Em, G, C, and A
sequence: Play the low E single-note motif on beats 1 through 4
Stab the chord on beats 5 and 6
Maintain tight palm muting for punchy low-end definition
tips: Kim Thayil and Chris Cornell both played in standard tuning for this track, unlike many other Drop D Soundgarden songs
Lock into Matt Cameron's snare drum to keep the 6/4 pulse natural and swaying
Don't rush the extra two beats in the 6/4 measure—let the groove breathe

techniques.name: Kim Thayil's Microtonal Wah Lead Phrasing & Dissonant Accents
techniques.description: Kim Thayil's signature avant-garde grunge solo style featuring unhinged Cry Baby wah filter sweeps, quarter-tone microtonal bends, and controlled feedback howling

notes: E blues scale in 12th position: frets 12-15 on strings 1, 2, and 3
Flat-5 blue note (15th fret G string / 14th fret D string) bent slightly sharp for dissonant friction
Full-step bends on the 15th fret B string matched to 12th fret high E
sequence: Rock the wah pedal slowly from heel to toe to highlight vocal harmonics
Execute singing whole-step and microtonal bends in 12th position
Incorporate controlled amplifier feedback between lead phrases
Lock back into the 6/4 rhythm riff on the downbeat
tips: Thayil played a vintage Guild S-100 through Peavey VTM-120 and Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier amps
Embrace intentional dissonance—the blue note flat-5 gives Soundgarden their trademark dark tension
Keep unpicked strings muted with the fretting-hand index finger flesh to prevent unwanted noise
details.progression: B5 - C5 - D5 - Em Solo Progression

sections.name: 6/4 Metric Main Riff & Palm-Muted Walkdown
sections.description: The brooding 6/4 riff that defines the song's hypnotic, off-kilter swing.
notes: Count 1-2-3-4-5-6 per measure
Tight palm muting on the low E string notes
Clean chord stab on beats 5 and 6

sections.name: Verse 1 Brooding 6/4 Rhythmic Groove
sections.description: Hypnotic verse backing Chris Cornell's somber, searching vocal melody.
notes: Maintain sludgy low-end clarity
Leave space for the vocal narrative
Accentuate the passing C note on the 5th string

sections.name: Chorus Wall of Sound & Dorian Lift
sections.description: Full wall-of-sound chorus ('Just like every day, fell on black days') lifting into the major IV chord (A).
notes: Massive overdriven strumming across all six strings
Notice the uplifting major A chord at the end of the phrase
Lock tight with the drum cymbals

sections.name: Bridge Rising Power Chords
sections.description: Stepwise ascending power chord bridge (B5 - C5 - D5) building tension into the guitar solo.
notes: Dig into root-5 power chords on frets 2, 3, and 5
Drive the tempo forward into the solo
Hit the final open Em chord with maximum authority

sections.name: Kim Thayil Guitar Solo (Microtonal Wah Bends)
sections.description: Kim Thayil's wild, expressive solo featuring screaming wah sweeps, flatted fifth dissonance, and howling sustain.
notes: 12th-position E blues pentatonic bends
Rock wah pedal slowly for sweeping vowel tones
Wring out aggressive, unhinged finger vibrato

sections.name: Outro Hypnotic 6/4 Chug & Vocal Cadence
sections.description: The hypnotic 6/4 riff cycles out under Cornell's soaring falsetto calls, ending on a sustained low E chord.
notes: Lock into Matt Cameron's final drum accents
Gradually loosen palm muting for heavier acoustic weight
Let the final low E minor chord ring into silence

guitar.recommended: 1970s Guild S-100 or Gibson Les Paul Custom
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for heavy, sludgy low-end grunge bite

amp.recommended: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier & Peavey VTM-120 through 4x12 cabs

effects.distortion: Amp high-gain tube distortion boosted by subtle overdrive
effects.wah: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah (used for microtonal solo sweeps)

beginner.title: Chorus Chords & Strumming
steps: Learn the four chorus chords: Em, G, C, and A
Recognize the major A chord that gives the chorus its Dorian color

intermediate.title: The 6/4 Metric Riff
steps: Internalize the 6-beat count: 4 beats of single notes + 2 beats of chord stabs
Coordinate the low E string walkdown with tight palm muting
Play along seamlessly with Matt Cameron's drum groove at 104 BPM

advanced.title: Full Arrangement & Kim Thayil Solo
steps: Learn Kim Thayil's microtonal wah solo and dissonant chord accents
Maintain relentless metric pocket across all dynamic changes
Capture the authentic Superunknown wall of sound live

commonMistakes: Trying to count the riff in 4/4 and dropping the last two beats of each bar
Playing G minor instead of G major in the chorus
Rushing the relaxed, heavy 104 BPM tempo
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: 6/4 counting drill out loud with metronome
5 minutes: Main riff low E single-note walkdown at 85 BPM → 104 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus open chord dynamic strumming
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 6/4 at 90 BPM, counting 1-2-3-4-5-6 with an accent on beat 1
